kicker_candidates: DRHP Analysis: A B Infrabuild Limited

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild wins contracts through a tender process: it bids for projects floated by government clients, and is typically awarded the lowest quote. [^drhp-p72]
The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and ready-mix concrete (RMC) manufacturing from its plant in Kashimira, Thane. [^drhp-p63] [^drhp-p71]
Revenue is heavily concentrated: Western Railway contributed 52% of the order book, and top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in Fiscal 2018. [^drhp-p65] [^drhp-p67]

The company lists competitive strengths including long-standing client relationships (Western Railway since 2006), use of modern techniques like box pushing, and a state-of-the-art RMC facility. [^drhp-p67]
Most operations are concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra. [^drhp-p67]

business.heading: What the Company Does
business.purpose: Explain the business model, revenue generation, contract process, customer concentration, and key strengths as disclosed.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, after peaking at ₹90.21 crore. [^drhp-p27]
Net profit after adjustments was erratic: ₹0.96 crore in FY2014, ₹0.78 crore in FY2015, ₹0.33 crore in FY2016, ₹0.16 crore in FY2017, then jumped to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018. [^drhp-p27]
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) was ₹9.46 crore in FY2015 and ₹9.29 crore in FY2018, with a dip in FY2017 to ₹6.76 crore. [^drhp-p111]
Long-term borrowings declined from ₹6.73 crore in FY2015 to ₹1.33 crore in FY2018, but short-term borrowings rose from ₹30.82 crore to ₹35.37 crore over the same period. [^drhp-p26]
Total assets grew from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014 to ₹82.32 crore in FY2018. [^drhp-p26]
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which could impact operations. [^drhp-p16]

financials.heading: Financial Performance
financials.purpose: Present revenue, profit, EBITDA, debt, and cash flow trends across all reported periods (FY2014 to FY2018) using restated financials. All figures in ₹ crore.

beats.beat: The promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, holds 7,495,476 equity shares — 90.949% of the pre-issue capital. [^drhp-p100]
Other directors (Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, Mukesh Pandey) each hold 300 shares. [^drhp-p93]
Key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori (aged 28, CA) and CS Mohit Soni (aged 26, ACS). [^drhp-p97]

Related-party transactions: loans taken from KMP/board of ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables of ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018. [^drhp-p129] [^drhp-p130]
No criminal cases or willful default declarations against directors or promoter are reported. [^drhp-p90] [^drhp-p100]
Governance red flags: two companies promoted by the promoter (Al-Noor Chickens and A B Magma Automobiles) were struck off by ROC for non-operation. [^drhp-p18]

governance.heading: Corporate Governance and Shareholding
governance.purpose: Describe promoter control, board, key management personnel, related-party transactions, and any governance flags noted in the filing.

beats.beat: The construction sector is highly fragmented and working capital intensive, contributing about 8% to India's GDP. [^drhp-p58]
Key demand drivers include government programs like 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, eased FDI norms, and rising urbanization. [^drhp-p58] [^drhp-p59]
The logistics sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020. [^drhp-p59]
The company faces competition from both organized and unorganized players. [^drhp-p76]
Acknowledged headwinds include slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies. [^drhp-p76]

industry.heading: Industry and Market
industry.purpose: Describe the infrastructure and construction market in India, key demand drivers, competition, and headwinds acknowledged by the company.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a Ready Mix Concrete plant. [^drhp-p63]
The company's major clients include Western Railways, Central Railways, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation, and MMRDA. [^drhp-p63]
It is offering 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each in a fresh issue; the price is to be determined. [^drhp-p29]
The proceeds will be used primarily to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes. [^drhp-p48]
The company is promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 90.949% of the pre-issue equity. [^drhp-p100]

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: A B Infrabuild is an infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete company based in Mumbai, raising funds via an SME IPO to meet working capital needs. Nearly all revenue comes from government and PSU clients, with Indian Railways as the dominant customer.

beats.beat: The issue comprises a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each; the price will be determined later. [^drhp-p29]
Lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited. [^drhp-p31]
The primary object is to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs). A portion is also allocated for general corporate purposes. [^drhp-p48]
The company has not appointed an independent agency for project appraisal, nor a monitoring agency; fund deployment will be monitored by the audit committee. [^drhp-p18]

offer.heading: The Offer and Use of Proceeds
offer.purpose: Detail the issue structure, purpose of the IPO, and key intermediaries.

beats.beat: Extreme customer concentration: Indian Railways (Western Railway) contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018 and 52% of the order book. Losing this client would cause a significant revenue dip. [^drhp-p12] [^drhp-p65]
Revenue depends on winning government tenders through a lowest-bid process; failure to secure contracts would materially affect financial condition. [^drhp-p12]
The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair operations if sustained. [^drhp-p16]
Unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakhs as of March 31, 2018 are repayable on demand; any recall could strain liquidity. [^drhp-p16]
Two promoter-held companies were struck off by the Registrar of Companies for non-operation, indicating past governance issues. [^drhp-p18]

beats.beat: The company's basic EPS (₹ per share) was 1.31 in FY2016, 0.63 in FY2017, and 12.59 in FY2018. [^drhp-p54]
Net asset value (NAV) per share (₹) was 4.14 in FY2016, 1.97 in FY2017, and 28.14 in FY2018. [^drhp-p54]
Return on net worth (RoNW) was 1% in FY2016, 2% in FY2017, and 3.82% in FY2018. [^drhp-p54]

The DRHP includes a comparison of accounting ratios with peer group companies, but the specific peer names and their ratios are not disclosed in the extracts available. Therefore, a peer P/E table cannot be constructed. [^drhp-p55]
